_about: Indicative cattle price anchors in Indian rupees. NOT a market survey and NOT live prices. Ranges come from dealer / breed-guide listings read in October 2026 (see sources). 'typical' is the geometric mean of low and high, rounded to the nearest 1,000. Edit this file, then run ml/scripts/make_synthetic_prices.py to regenerate the synthetic dataset and web/src/lib/price-anchors.generated.ts.
per_litre_note: ASSUMPTION. One Karnataka project report prices a crossbred cow at Rs 110,000 for 25 litres/day, i.e. about Rs 4,400 per litre of daily yield (own arithmetic, one data point, crossbred not indigenous). Rounded down to 4,000. Not measured on indigenous breeds.
pregnancy_note: Ratio of the pregnancy effect (1,114.07) to the milk-yield effect (719.54 per litre) in Kumar et al. (2014), Indian J. Animal Sciences 84(11), Table 2. Only the ratio is used, not those 2010-11 rupee amounts.

default.basis: No price source was found for this breed. This is the general desi-cow range: the median of the typical values of the breeds that do have a listed range, with the Tharparkar/Rathi range as its bounds.

Rathi.note: One dealer-guide figure for Rathi alone is 45,000 to 60,000.

Ongole.note: Ongole is mainly a draught breed; show and export animals sell far higher.

kamdhenu.title: Desi Cow Milk Per Day: 13 Indian Breeds Compared (2026), Kamdhenu Gauveda Team, 3 Oct 2026
kamdhenu.checked: Page fetched and read on 26 Oct 2026. A breed-guide table, not transaction data.

corroboration: Mahalakshmi Dairy Farm, Karnal (dealer): Gir about 1,00,000-1,25,000; Sahiwal and Tharparkar about 40,000-60,000 (https://www.exportersindia.com/maha-laxmi-dairy-farm/livestock.htm). Seen in search-result summaries only.
TradeIndia: Rathi 45,000-60,000 (https://www.tradeindia.com/question-answer/how-much-does-the-rathi-cow-cost/); Gir listings about 35,000-85,000. Seen in search-result summaries only.
Pashushala: Tharparkar listings 20,000-1,40,000 (https://www.pashushala.com/page/category/category?category=Cow&breed=Tharparkar). Seen in search-result summaries only.
A guide notes a cow bought at the breeding tract can cost much more after transport to a city, and a recorded-pedigree cow can sell for 50-70% more than an unrecorded one with the same milk.
not_modelled: Bulls and draught animals (for example Kangayam bulls Rs 40,000-70,000 at a village fair, up to 1-1.5 lakh for strong bloodlines; Hallikar and Ongole bullocks). The estimator assumes a milch cow.
Pedigree and milk-record premiums, region, season, age, lactation stage, and the animal's condition.
